Xibo CMS before 4.5.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other DataSets' RSS feeds by pairing their own DataSet id with a foreign RSS id. Attackers with dataset.modify permission can read, edit, or delete feeds and steal PSKs, then use the unauthenticated /rss/{psk} endpoint to exfiltrate victim DataSet rows.

Rootways Authorize.net CIM Pro extension for Magento 2 before 4.1.5 contains an unauthenticated server-side request forgery vulnerability in the Apple Pay merchant validation controller. Attackers can supply file://, gopher://, or dict:// URLs in the validationUrl parameter to read app/etc/env.php credentials and encryption keys or reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in coap_remove_observer_by_uri() that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read past the supplied URI buffer. Attackers can send a CoAP GET Observe request with a Uri-Path shorter than an existing observer's URL, causing memcmp with strlen to read beyond the non-NUL-terminated buffer.

Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an out-of-bounds access vulnerability in buffer_reclaim() and domain_set_free() in mpl.c that iterate the seed_set array one element past its end. Remote attackers can flood MPL multicast messages to fill the buffered message set, triggering out-of-bounds reads and writes of adjacent static memory that cause memory corruption or a crash.

Weblate 2026.11 through 2026.11.2 contains a time-of-check time-of-use race condition in the GET /api/tasks/{pk}/ endpoint that exposes unredacted repository error messages. Authenticated project members lacking vcs.view permission can poll failing repository tasks to obtain RepositoryCommandError text revealing upstream repository URLs, filesystem paths, and host names.

Bludit is vulnerable to Path Traversal in the page deletion functionality. An authenticated user with the Author role can set the UUID field of their own page to contain path traversal sequences (.. and path separators), which are saved without proper validation. When the page is deleted, Pages::delete() passes the path constructed from this UUID to Filesystem::deleteRecursive() without verifying that it still points to an allowed directory, allowing the attacker to delete any files, even not belonging to them. Critically, it is possible to delete admin pages and render the site unusable. Because vendor contact attempts were unsuccessful, the vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.22.0 but may also affect other versions.

Zammad before 7.2.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated customers to delete agents' shared ticket drafts by supplying a shared_draft_id. Attackers can create tickets via POST /api/v1/tickets or reply to accessible tickets referencing a draft id, destroying draft text prepared by agents.

The WP Abstracts plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.6. This is due to a missing capability check on the wpabs_save_regform AJAX action and the use of a static, frontend-exposed nonce that allows any authenticated user to persist attacker-controlled form schemas with arbitrary wpSync mappings that are later used as user meta keys in the wpabstracts_sync_wpfields function. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to elevate their privileges to administrator.

When changing the settings of a scheduled export, no permission checks are done to see whether the user making the change has access to the exporter after the change. This way, an attacker with access to change organizer settings and e.g. access to all orders could change the export to refer to gift cards instead, even if they do not have access to gift cards. The fix for this is technically a breaking API change, since changing the export type of existing scheduled exports is no longer allowed, but we don't expect this to affect any typical API usage.

Our WordPress plugin for the pretix Widget performs HTTP calls to pre-fetch CSS and JS files into a local cache and stores them publicly on the WordPress instance. These HTTP calls are made with wp_remote_get, not wp_safe_remote_get, and therefore allow SSRF with body extraction. Exploiting this requires sufficient WordPress permissions to create or modify pages.

pretixSCAN Proxy does not use a secure random generator to generate initialization tokens and API keys for the connection between pretixSCAN devices and the pretixSCAN Proxy. This could allow a skilled attacker with access to at least some of the tokens to predict the value of other tokens more easily. pretixSCAN is usually used on local networks and the level of exposure heavily depends on the structure of that network. If you want to be extra careful, it might make sense to reconnect your devices to the proxy after the update.

pretix provides a mechanism where ticket QR codes are cryptographically signed and can be verified by our pretixSCAN apps in offline mode without any database of valid tickets. pretixSCAN checks the signature to verify that the ticket was issued by the correct pretix event and compares the QR code against a list of revoked QR codes. A QR code becomes revoked when the order is canceled, or the ticket is changed in a way that a new QR code needs to be generated. However, the parsing of the QR code in all of our pretixSCAN apps contained a faulty computation, rendering the check for the correct length of the contents faulty. This way, an attacker is able to craft multiple QR codes for the same ticket which have the same content, but look different and therefore do not match against the revocation list. This does not allow to fabricate entirely new tickets, but it does allow to enter the event with e.g. a canceled ticket. This attack requires pretixSCAN to be scanning in offline mode and the "pretix signature scheme 1" to be used for the event's QR codes. If the attack is executed, the ticket unfortunately shows as valid (green) on the scanner but as invalid (red) on the server since the server later cannot match it to a ticket. We scanned the entire database of scans on pretix Hosted and could not find any traces of this being exploited in the past.

This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HMIS due to insufficient server side object level authorization validation in the API endpoint. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by modifying the parameter value in the API request. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to enumerate and gain unauthorized access to sensitive information of patients on the targeted healthcare organization.

This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HIMS due to the use of a static and predictable value in the client-side password hashing mechanism, which is embedded in the login page and accessible to unauthenticated users. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by accessing the login page, extracting the embedded value and using it to reproduce the password hashing process. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could weaken the security of the authentication mechanism and potentially facilitate authentication related attacks on the targeted healthcare organization.

This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HMIS due to the exposure of internal hospital operational statistics through data structure embedded in the HTML response of the login page. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by accessing the affected login page and extracting the returned HTML content. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to gain unauthorized access to internal hospital operational information associated with the targeted healthcare organization.

This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HMIS due to insufficient authentication and session validation in the dashboard functionality. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted HTTP requests to the affected endpoint. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to gain unauthorized access to the dashboard information associated with the targeted healthcare organization.

Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester. This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled. Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 processes XML external entities in software repository files. An attacker able to supply or modify the repository files received by the server can read files accessible to the N-central service account or cause the server to make outbound requests.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not validate version values and download locations in software update metadata. An attacker able to supply or modify the update metadata received by the server can write files outside the download directory and execute code as the N-central service account.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not verify that an action response received over XMPP originates from the appliance the request was sent to. An attacker with the credentials of one appliance can forge responses on behalf of another appliance.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not validate connection targets in the Report Manager and Data Export settings. An authenticated attacker can cause the server to connect to arbitrary hosts, including loopback and internal addresses, and can use the responses to probe internal network services.

The custom service import in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 processes XML external entities. An authenticated attacker can upload a crafted service definition to read files accessible to the N-central service account or cause the server to make outbound requests.

The test email delivery function in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not check permissions, lacks CSRF protection, and passes sender and recipient values to the mail program without neutralising option characters. An authenticated attacker can inject arguments into the mail command executed on the server.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 checks only a view permission for ServerII2 operations that write device execution configuration. An authenticated user with view-only access to a device can set configuration that the Windows agent on that device acts on.

Multiple ServerUI and ServerUI2 SOAP operations in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 do not verify the caller's session, permissions or customer scope. A remote attacker, in some cases without authentication, can read device and patch data, test passwords of user accounts, send messages to managed agents, and modify device and service settings belonging to other customers.

The password reset function in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 returns distinguishable responses for valid and invalid accounts. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can enumerate the email addresses of valid user accounts.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the ServerII2 remoteControlMSPAStartEndTimeSubmit operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can alter the recorded state and times of Take Control remote control tasks and the associated audit log entries.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the MaintActionGet operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can read and cancel the pending maintenance actions of any appliance.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the ServerMMS2 AssetDiscoSimplifiedInfoSubmit operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can overwrite the asset data recorded for any appliance.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 allows the repositoryItemGet operation to be called without authentication. A remote, unauthenticated attacker who knows a policy identifier can download the Automation Manager policy of any customer, including embedded scripts and parameter values.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the ServerMMS2 RemoteExecutionTaskSubmit operation or verify task ownership. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can submit forged results for remote execution tasks belonging to any customer.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not neutralise control characters in an Audit Export setting before writing it to the system logging configuration. An authenticated attacker with product administrator privileges can inject configuration and execute commands as root on the N-central server.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 uses a predictable credential to authenticate appliances to an agent-facing API. A remote, unauthenticated attacker who knows or guesses an appliance identifier can obtain a valid appliance token and session and impersonate that appliance.
The Patch Management Engine in N-central is vulnerable to LPE via attacker controlled metadata

The RSS widget of the dashboard allows backend users to configure the URL of the RSS feed in the widget settings. The URL was fetched by the server without restricting the target host. Backend users with access to the dashboard could therefore make the server send HTTP requests to arbitrary hosts, including internal network services and cloud metadata endpoints, which are not reachable from the outside.

The file dump controller (eID=dumpFile) delivers files, file references and processed files identified by their uid, protected by a token. The token only covered the uid value, but not the type of the requested resource. A valid token issued for a file could therefore be reused to request a file reference or a processed file with the same uid. As a result, unauthenticated visitors could download files, for example from non-public storages, for which no token had been issued.

The FileUpload and ImageUpload elements of the Form Framework use the property allowedMimeTypes as an allow list of MIME types accepted for upload. An empty allowedMimeTypes list was treated as "no restriction". Forms containing upload elements without any configured MIME type, for example in manually created form definitions or when all MIME types were deselected in the form editor, accepted any file except those blocked by the file deny pattern, which only covers PHP-related file extensions. This allowed unauthenticated users to upload files with browser-executable content, such as HTML or SVG documents, to the configured upload folder, which by default is located in a public storage. If attackers know the URL of an uploaded file (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-029), this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder.

The cHash argument, which ensures that only URL arguments originally generated by TYPO3 create separate page cache entries, was treated inconsistently when it was passed as an array. The cHash validation treated such a value as missing, while the page cache identifier treated it as present and included all URL arguments. As a result, unauthenticated visitors could create an unlimited number of page cache entries and trigger uncached page renderings by adding an array cHash with arbitrary values to any URL. This could exhaust server resources and fill the page cache storage. Only installations where the cHash validation is not enforced via $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['FE']['cacheHash']['enforceValidation'] are affected. This setting is enabled by default for new installations since TYPO3 v12, but is often still disabled in installations upgraded from older versions.

The fix for TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-009 was incomplete. GeneralUtility::sanitizeLocalUrl performed its checks on the URL-decoded value, but returned the original, URL-encoded value. URLs containing certain percent-encoded characters therefore passed the sanitization checks as local URLs, although they point to an external host. Applications that use the sanitized URL for redirects are vulnerable to open redirect attacks. This enables attackers to redirect users to external content and carry out phishing attacks. In the TYPO3 core, this affects redirects in the backend, which require the victim to be logged in to the backend.

Files uploaded through FileUpload or ImageUpload elements are stored in an unguessable sub-folder that remains the same for the whole form session. If storing an uploaded file failed, for example because of a file name exceeding the file system's length limit, the raw error message was shown to the frontend user disclosing the storage path including the unguessable folder name and the server's temporary upload directory. With this information, attackers could determine the public URL of files they upload through the form. If a form allows uploading files that browsers can execute, such as HTML documents, this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder. This vulnerability is known to be actively exploited.

ImageMagick and GraphicsMagick use small modules, called "coders", to read each image format. When processing images, TYPO3 determined the coder from the file type detected by the file contents, as long as the detected mime-type started with image/. A file containing MVG (Magick Vector Graphics) instructions, uploaded with an image file extension like .png, was therefore processed with the MVG coder. MVG instructions can read local files into the processed image, which allows disclosing the contents of arbitrary files readable by the web server, for example configuration files containing credentials, through a publicly accessible processed image. Exploiting this vulnerability requires a way to upload files without a mime-type check, for example a public form of the Form Framework using a FileUpload or ImageUpload element without configured allowedMimeTypes (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-032), which allows exploitation by unauthenticated visitors. Additionally, ImageMagick must be used for image processing, and its default system configuration must allow the MVG coder.

The installer (first installation wizard) could be re-enabled on an already configured instance by placing a file whose name starts with FIRST_INSTALL in the public web root or the project root. The installer then became accessible without authentication, allowing for example to change the database connection and to create a new administrator and system maintainer account, which leads to remote code execution. As demonstrated in TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-026, such a file could be created by an authenticated, low-privileged backend user without any further permissions. Other ways of creating files in the web root, as well as leftover or restored marker files, could be abused in the same way. With the fixed versions, the installer can no longer be re-enabled on an already configured instance by a marker file. A new internal setting $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['SYS']['isInstalling'] is stored in the system configuration and is only enabled while a new installation is running. Additionally, only the exact file names FIRST_INSTALL and FIRST_INSTALL.txt are accepted as marker files.

The backend endpoint for adding online media (e.g. YouTube or Vimeo videos) accepted a target folder in the fallback storage (storage uid 0), which points to the public web root of the installation. File mount and permission checks are not applied to the fallback storage. As a result, any authenticated, low-privileged backend user, even without file mounts or module access, could create online media files with a partially controllable file name in the public web root. In combination with TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-027, this could be used to re-enable the installer on an already configured instance. The installer could then be used to create a new administrator and system maintainer account, which leads to remote code execution.

When importing a T3D or XML file in the Import/Export module, the file hash values of imported files were taken from the import data without validation and used to build the path of a temporary file. A crafted import file could therefore write files with arbitrary content to any location writable by the web server, for example a PHP file in the public web root, which leads to remote code execution. Exploiting this vulnerability requires an administrator backend user account, or a non-admin backend user for whom importing has been enabled via the user TSconfig option options.impexp.enableImportForNonAdminUser.

This High severity Improper Authorization vulnerability was introduced in versions 5.12.0, 10.3.0, and 11.3.0 of Jira Service Management Data Center. This Improper Authorization vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 7.1, allows an authenticated attacker to gain unintended access and can lead to the exposure of resources or functionality, possibly providing attackers with sensitive information or even execute arbitrary code. Atlassian recommends that Jira Service Management Data Center customers upgrade to latest version, if you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to one of the specified supported fixed versions: Jira Service Management Data Center 10.3: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 10.3.27 Jira Service Management Data Center 11.3: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 11.3.13 See the release notes (https://confluence.atlassian.com/servicemanagement/jira-service-management-release-notes-780083086.html). You can download the latest version of Jira Service Management Data Center from the download center (https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/service-management/download-archives). This vulnerability was reported via our Bug Bounty program.

The CODESYS Automation Server Connector uses server-supplied file names without sufficient path traversal checks. An unauthenticated remote attacker controlling a malicious Automation Server and tricking a user to trust it, or performing a man-in-the-middle attack on a trusted communication channel, can exploit this vulnerability to write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary locations on the engineering workstation and subsequently achieve arbitrary code execution with user privileges.

The affected products do not sufficiently validate CODESYS Automation Server TLS certificates when a user starts the certificate enrollment. An unauthenticated remote attacker performing a man-in-the-middle attack can exploit this vulnerability by supplying an untrusted certificate that is accepted as trusted. Successful exploitation may allow an attacker to intercept and manipulate communications between the CODESYS Automation Server and the PLC network.

The affected products process a server-supplied URL without sufficient validation. An unauthenticated remote attacker controlling a malicious Automation Server and tricking a user to trust it or performing a man-in-the-middle attack, can exploit this vulnerability by causing the affected product to process unintended content. Successful exploitation may result in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running the affected product.

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability reflected in the GET parameters `cod_primaria` and `cod_secundaria` of the Novanet Web endpoints `NNws_ShwNewDup` and `NPcd/NFG_VerNoticia`. User-provided data is reflected within a JavaScript block without proper sanitization or context-appropriate output encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker could craft a manipulated URL that, when visited by a victim, would execute arbitrary JavaScript code in the victim’s browser, within the context of the affected site. The flaw resides in the platform’s shared code, so it could affect organizations using that vulnerable code.

Issue summary: A server configured with the Suite B certificate flag through SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() and with TLS 1.3 enabled may read past the end of a fixed group list when it processes a ClientHello whose supported_groups and key_share contain no Suite B group. Impact summary: A remote client can send a ClientHello that makes the server read past the end of a static array. The values read are never returned to the client, so no memory is disclosed; on builds with sanitizers or hardened allocators the read may crash the process, causing Denial of Service. CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read Description: When the Suite B certificate flag is set, OpenSSL restricts the accepted groups to P-256 and P-384 by substituting a fixed two-element list for the configured group list. The tuple machinery used for key-share selection was not updated for this substitution: tls1_get_group_tuples() still returns the configured tuples, which by default describe eight groups. The server-side walk in tls_parse_ctos_key_share() then advances through the two-element list using those tuple counts without checking the cumulative offset against the number of groups present. Only applications that call SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() with SSL_CERT_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS and leave TLS 1.3 enabled are affected. The openssl s_server -suiteB_128 option sets an X.509 verification parameter instead, so the stock command line server is not vulnerable. Default configurations do not reach this code. A client that offers only groups outside the Suite B set, such as X25519, forces every tuple to be walked and the read to run past the array. The bytes read are compared against client group IDs and never sent back, so no memory is disclosed. On builds with address sanitizers or hardened allocators the read can abort the process; in ordinary release builds it reads a few bytes of adjacent constant data. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection if the peer resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even though the peer's stream credit is returned. Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC handshake can repeatedly open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow without bound until the process runs out of memory and every connection on it is lost. This is a Denial of Service. CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer opens. When the incoming stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a STOP_SENDING frame, marks the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A deleted stream is collected only once its receive part is fully drained, which for a rejected stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If the peer sends RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending STOP_SENDING, so it is never sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected. The default configuration reaches this path. Once a connection has a default stream, meaning the application has read from or written to the connection as the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream policy rejects streams the application does not accept. Applications that set the REJECT policy explicitly are affected too. Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's stream credit window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that keeps the connection open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server memory without bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a long-lived connection, and causes no memory corruption or disclosure. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

In nanobot, the WebSocket gateway allows a standard client holding a valid client token to select an existing directory outside the operator-configured workspace as the root of a new conversation. The agent can then read and expose files in that directory that are readable by the nanobot service account. This issue affects nanobot (nanobot-ai) from 0.3.5 before 0.4.1.

In nanobot, when sandboxed exec is enabled, the shell executable used to run commands can be selected by the caller and is launched before the sandbox is applied. An attacker who can induce the agent to create an executable in the workspace and select it as the shell can cause that executable to run outside the sandbox (e.g. Linux bubblewrap), with the operating-system permissions of the nanobot process. This issue affects nanobot (nanobot-ai) from 0.2.1 before 0.4.1.

The MembershipWorks - Membership, Events & Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in all versions up to, and including, 6.17. This is due to insufficient output escaping on member-supplied data retrieved from the MembershipWorks SaaS API in the sf_shortcode(), sf_widget_event_do(), and sf_widget_folder_do() functions, where the 'nam' (member name), 'ttl' (event title), 'url', 'adn' (venue name), 'szp', and 'ezp' fields are output into page HTML without escaping, or, in sf_widget_folder_do(), placed in an image alt attribute that an onerror handler copies into innerHTML. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

In the Matter door lock applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, AccessManager::ValidateCredential() checks only credential occupancy and the secret bytes, and never reads the owning user's UserStatus. It also returns success when no owning user can be resolved. A user suspended by setting their status to OccupiedDisabled can continue to unlock the door with their previously assigned credential, and an orphaned but occupied credential is also accepted. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In the Matter and Aliro Door Lock Application of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1 with CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE enabled, deleting a Credential Issuer passes the 1-based Matter credential index to ClearValidityIterations(), which expects a 0-based storage index. The intended issuer's ValidityIteration state is left in place, and the state of the adjacent, still-provisioned issuer is cleared. This resets that issuer's rollback protection. An attacker holding an older but correctly signed Access Document from the adjacent issuer, whose validity iteration had been superseded, can then potentially obtain physical access. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In the Aliro access control reference applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, the stored Access Document record does not retain validFrom and validUntil. The cached public key path (VerifyPublicKey()) and the Kpersistent fast path (_VerifyKPersistentKey()) therefore never re-evaluate the Access Document validity period. An attacker who held a time-limited Aliro credential that was valid when first presented can continue to obtain physical access after the Access Document has expired, for as long as the cached record remains available. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In the Aliro access control reference applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, built with Credential Issuer CA certificate-based issuer trust (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_ISSUER_CA) and the Aliro Step-up phase (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE) enabled, AccessManagerImpl::ProcessValidityIteration() treats a failed lookup of the Credential Issuer in the provisioned issuer array as success. For an issuer trusted through a certificate chain but not provisioned, the ValidityIteration (credential-rollback) check is therefore skipped. A former authorized holder with an old but correctly issuer-signed Access Document can be granted physical access after the issuer has advanced its iteration to revoke that credential. The default Matter provisioning configuration is not affected. Fixed in v1.2.0.

Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails, OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones and any new ones, but leaves them in the stack. Impact summary: An application that passes an existing stack to PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a failed read may use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash or, in principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make the read fail, but only applications that pass an existing stack are affected, and OpenSSL itself does not do this. CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads certificates, CRLs and private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of X509_INFO structures. If the application passes a stack that is not NULL, the function adds the new entries to it and must leave the entries that are already there unchanged. If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the stack. This includes the entries that were there before the call, and the entries added by the call. It does not remove these entries from the stack, so the stack keeps pointers to freed memory. The failure can happen at any point, even before any entry was added. A PEM item with invalid content is enough. This also happens if the stack was empty: entries added before the failure are freed but stay in the stack. An application that then reads or frees the stack will use memory that was already freed. This can crash the application or, in principle, corrupt memory. Only applications that pass a stack that is not NULL are affected. OpenSSL itself never does this. Its own callers, including the code that TLS uses to load CA certificates, always pass NULL. When the stack is NULL, the function frees only the entries that it created itself, which is safe. We expect that very few applications pass an existing stack. An attacker can make the read fail with malformed PEM data, but cannot make an application pass an existing stack. The same problem affects PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(), PEM_X509_INFO_read() and PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex(), which use the same code. OpenSSL 1.1.1 and 1.0.2 have only the first two of these functions. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Cool Plugins Conditional Fields for Elementor Form – Display Conditions conditional-fields-for-elementor-form allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Conditional Fields for Elementor Form – Display Conditions: from n/a through 1.7.7.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in LeapWorx Premium Addons for Elementor premium-addons-for-elementor allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Premium Addons for Elementor: from n/a through 4.11.118.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in WPExperts Gutena Forms – Contact Form, Survey Form, Feedback Form, Booking Form, and Custom Form Builder gutena-forms allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Gutena Forms – Contact Form, Survey Form, Feedback Form, Booking Form, and Custom Form Builder: from n/a through 2.1.1.

The All in One SEO – AI SEO Plugin to Boost SEO Rankings & Traffic (Schema, Local SEO, Sitemap & SEO Insights) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that an administrator has placed the AIOSEO breadcrumb on the author template, that the site is running WordPress 6.6 or later with the core Interactivity runtime loaded (e.g., via a block theme or core/navigation block), and that a victim clicks the rendered breadcrumb link on the author archive page.

Joomla Extension - valorapps.com - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in Easy File Uploader < 2.9.7 - An unauthenticated remote attacker can upload a PHP-executable file to the Joomla web root with a single multipart POST request, requiring no credentials and no CSRF token.

The RSS Feed Retriever WordPress plugin through 1.6.10 does not validate a user-supplied URL before fetching it server-side with a bundled HTTP library that lacks WordPress's private-network protections, allowing unauthenticated users to make the site retrieve arbitrary internal or external resources and read the response.

The Everest Backup – WordPress Cloud Backup, Migration, Restore & Cloning Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.14 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to activate any already-installed inactive plugin on the site.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.4 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user holding an MCP-scoped OAuth token to perform unauthorized issuable state changes on issues and merge requests, including approving and merging, due to incorrect authorization checks.

The Soledad theme for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7.7 The public penci_more_post_ajax AJAX action feeds infeedads[ads_code] (base64+urldecoded) to penci_safe_shortcode(), whose allowlist regex inspects only the hyphen-truncated outer shortcode name (e.g. 'adinserter') and never the nested [elementor-element k=.. data=..] tag, so do_shortcode() renders an attacker-chosen Elementor element. The rendered penci-featured-sliders widget passes its unsanitized 'style' setting to include dirname(__FILE__)."/{$style}.php", a path-traversal local file inclusion.
